summary: Cupola cabin on Goat Mountain, Boundary County, ID (Kaniksu NF), dated 1924; destroyed or gone 1965; one staff name (1933-35); a 2024-updated article lists a concrete box on the mountain.

facts.status_note: Destroyed or gone in 1965 per all three listings; a concrete box on Goat Mountain is listed among remnants of other lookouts, not tied to this one by name

visit.trail_note: Idaho Fire Lookouts lists the site as hike-in; no source describes current access

events.note: Listed as a cupola cabin dated 1924
Charley Forslund listed as lookout personnel for 1933 to 1935
Destroyed in 1965 per Rex's page and Idaho Fire Lookouts; Forest Lookouts lists it as gone in 1965
Boundary County lookout article, updated June 2024, lists a concrete box on Goat Mountain among remnants of other lookouts

evidence.supports: about 13 miles northeast of Bonners Ferry, Boundary County
Forest Lookouts listing, township and range 63N-3E-34
remnants of other lookouts, including a concrete box on Goat Mountain
evidence.quote: Remnants still remain of others, such as concrete footings on the Mollies, Smith Peak, and a concrete box on Goat Mountain.

evidence.supports: article first published March 2011, updated June 2024

sources.title: Fire Lookouts of Boundary County, Idaho

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Rex's page and Idaho Fire Lookouts say destroyed in 1965; Forest Lookouts says gone in 1965. The year agrees, so the story gives 1965 and notes both words.

notes_for_editor: Brief has two coordinate sets (ffla 48.7778,-116.05948 and idaho_fl 48.77311,-116.05292), about 0.7 km apart. No source read gives coordinates, so the conflict is unresolved and the brief's coordinates are left unchanged. Do not merge with a different lookout also called Goat Mtn: idahofirelookouts.com/st-joe-clearwater-region/goat-mtn/ describes a St. Joe NF tower (elevation 6155, 1916 crow's nest, 1934 pole tower with L-4 cab, destroyed 1961, patrol point on Blackdome). A guessed NHLR URL for this lookout returned 404. Brief access 'unknown' kept, so no access key. Six distinct pages read and one WebSearch. The only site-today description is the single 2011/2024 article, which does not name this lookout.
